summary: version-anchor oscillation during staged traffic shear causes transparent degrade to backup variant
description:
Issue summary: During a staged weighted traffic shear for tenant clearpath-health, a subset of requests drifted from the intended version-anchor and were transparently routed to the fallback (degraded) variant without explicit error or an increase in 5xx counts. Behavior observed during a 20%->40% traffic shear window.

What happened: The serving mesh experienced repeated short-lived reassignments of the tenant's version-anchor (oscillation). When a request hit an orchestrator epoch where the anchor did not match the edge replica's local pin state, the routing decision fell back to the backup variant. Because the responses were valid, the customer application saw correct responses but with degraded latency and quality compared to the pinned model.

Why this is critical: ClearPath Health uses model pinning for deterministic clinical prompts; silent routing to a degraded variant can change output quality and violates expected model guarantees. The customer noticed increased subtle hallucinations and higher token latency for a subset of requests.
impact: Approximately 4.7% of tenant requests during the shear window were served by the fallback variant. Customer reported quality regressions on clinical summarization workflows and increased per-request latency (~120ms median increase). No 5xx spike; business impact is data integrity risk for clinical customers.

2026-03-13 09:17 UTC - Customer Slack #support-msg: reports of lower-quality summaries and slight latency increase
2026-03-13 09:20 UTC - Observability alert: small latency bump in edge-proxy per-tenant histogram (us-east)

environment_details: Prod control plane (managed) with dedicated GPU pool for customer. Edge proxies in us-east fronting orchestrator shards. Orchestrator version: v1.21.3; serving runtime: v3.6.2 (KV cache enabled); edge-proxy: v2.9.1. Canary config used: staged shear with prewarm replicas. Pin model: rwft-7b-quant@2026-03-10-abc123. Backup variant: rwft-7b-quant-compat@2026-02-28-compat.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create tenant-scoped rollout in staging that mimics production staged shear (20->40% over 10 minutes)
2) Prewarm target replicas and ensure orchestrator and edge-proxy epoch counters are unsynchronized (simulate small clock skew by delaying edge heartbeat)
3) Issue high QPS tenant-scoped requests with pinned-version header set and observe per-request routing decisions via debug route header X-Redwood-Variant
4) Monitor for short-lived variant flips correlated to orchestrator epoch boundary events
logs_and_metrics: Edge-proxy logs show routing decisions where X-Requested-Version header present but local pin_lookup returned stale anchor; orchestrator log lines indicate "epoch_consensus=failed" and epoch mismatch at 09:16:47 UTC. Per-tenant routing histograms show a transient shift of ~4-5% of requests to backup variant. KV cache hit-rate stayed stable. No 5xx in the period; token latency histogram shows a tail shift. Relevant log excerpts saved to S3: s3://redwood-support/logs/SUP-482410/epoch-mismatch-09-16.log
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Orchestrator-Edge epoch handshake timing plus staged shear increases the chance of local pin state being sampled pre-commit, causing fallback routing when the orchestrator later commits a different anchor.
Hypothesis B: Prewarm mirror write path may not immediately reconcile local replica pin cache; combined with rapid weight change (shear) this surfaces oscillation.
Reproduced in staging when artificially delaying edge heartbeat by 200-500ms and running 150 qps of tenant-scoped traffic. Observed same transparent degrade pattern.
Checked related subsystems: TTLs for anchor cache are 12s; commit window is 2s; under shear the commit cadence increases — race observed between commit window and TTL refresh.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-13 09:30 - Notified customer and escalated to SRE; initial mitigation planned: pause staged shear and increase pin commit atomicy window.

Diego Martinez (SRE) 2026-03-13 09:38 - Confirmed reproduction in staging; proposing short-term mitigation: hold anchor TTL at 30s for affected tenants during shear and add an epoch-stability check before allowing fallback routing.
Emma Li (Serving Runtime) 2026-03-13 10:05 - Noted that prewarm mirror path does an eventual write; will add fast-path reconcile for tenant-scoped pin writes. Will submit PR for review.
Customer (ClearPath Health) 2026-03-13 10:12 - Customer acked rollback and requested follow-up on guardrails to guarantee no silent fallback during clinical runs.
short_term_mitigation: Rolled back staged shear and temporarily increased anchor TTL to 30s for ClearPath Health tenant. Added an observability rule to alert on any cryptic variant assignment without 5xx. Notified customer and applied hold on further rollouts until fix lands.
long_term_action_items: 1) Orchestrator: introduce epoch-stability handshake — require 2 consecutive epoch-aligned heartbeats before allowing a variant change for pinned tenants.
2) Serving runtime: fast-path reconcile for prewarm mirror write to update local pin cache immediately on commit.
3) Console: add rollout guardrail that disallows staged shear >X%/minute for pinned tenants (configurable by customer tier).
4) Postmortem: runbook update and customer-facing summary to be produced within 3 business days.
resolution: In progress. Short-term rollback and TTL extension stopped further customer impact. Engineering PRs opened: github.com/redwood-inference/coordination/pull/1128 (epoch-stability) and github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/2043 (fast-path reconcile). Target deploy calendar: canary 2026-03-16, global 2026-03-18 after verification in staging. Postmortem scheduled.
follow_up_notes: Customer requested enforceable guardrail to prevent silent fallback for tenants with clinical SLAs. CS and Solutions will offer options: automatic no-fallback mode for pinned tenants or stricter rollout rate limits.
